title: The AI Work Kit
subtitle: 25 practical prompts + 5 plug-and-play workflows to help you use AI like a coworker.
quickStart: Pick one task you need to finish today — not a vague goal.
Choose the closest prompt or workflow in this kit.
Replace every [bracketed placeholder] with your real context.
Give the AI examples, constraints, and the format you want back.
Review the result. Ask for one specific improvement instead of starting over.

toolCheatSheet.task: Research that needs current web sources
toolCheatSheet.tool: A web-connected AI or search/research tool

toolCheatSheet.task: Long documents and careful document analysis
toolCheatSheet.tool: Claude / ChatGPT with the source file attached
Your preferred AI plus an automation platform

sections.name: Writing & communication
prompts: Rewrite this so it sounds clear, confident, and human. Keep my meaning, remove filler, and keep it under [length]: [paste text].
Draft a reply to this message. My goal is [goal], my tone should be [tone], and I do not want to say or promise [constraint]: [paste message].
Turn these rough notes into a finished [email/post/document]. Put the most important point first and end with a clear next step: [notes].
Edit this in two passes. First fix clarity and structure. Then tighten the language without making it sound robotic: [paste text].
Give me three versions of this message: direct, warm, and persuasive. Preserve the facts exactly: [paste message].

sections.name: Research & learning
prompts: Teach me [topic] from zero. Start with the mental model I need first, use one everyday example, then give me three things to learn next.
Research [question]. Separate verified facts, reasonable inferences, and open questions. Cite sources for claims that could have changed.
I need to understand this quickly: [paste text]. Give me the five most important points, define unfamiliar terms, and tell me what deserves a closer look.
Compare [option A] and [option B] for this situation: [context]. Use the criteria [criteria] and show where the evidence is uncertain.
Quiz me on [topic] one question at a time. Adjust difficulty based on my answers and explain mistakes simply.

sections.name: Business & decisions
prompts: Turn this business idea into a one-page plan covering customer, problem, offer, acquisition channel, revenue model, biggest assumption, and first test: [idea].
Act as a skeptical customer. Review this offer and tell me what is unclear, unbelievable, unnecessary, or missing: [offer].
I need to decide [decision]. Build a decision table using these priorities: [priorities]. Ask me for missing facts before reaching a conclusion.
Find the weakest assumption in this plan and design the cheapest test that could prove or disprove it within [time/budget]: [plan].
Turn these customer comments into themes. Identify repeated problems, desired outcomes, exact phrases worth preserving, and possible offers: [feedback].

sections.name: Content & creation
prompts: Turn this idea into 10 content angles for [platform]. Avoid repeating the same hook. Target [audience] and drive toward [CTA]: [idea].
Write five hooks for this topic using different structures: surprising fact, problem, contrarian question, story opening, and specific outcome: [topic].
Repurpose this long piece into one short video script, one carousel outline, one email, and three short posts without copying sentences word-for-word: [content].
Review this content for attention drop-offs. Mark where a viewer is likely to leave and rewrite those sections to create forward momentum: [script].
Build a seven-day content plan around [theme]. Each day needs a distinct angle, format, opening hook, and CTA.

sections.name: Productivity & automation
prompts: Here are my tasks: [list]. Rank them by impact, urgency, effort, and dependency, then build a realistic plan for [time available].
Break this repeated task into trigger, inputs, decisions, actions, human approvals, outputs, and failure cases: [task].
Turn this messy process into a standard operating procedure that someone else could follow without asking me questions: [process].
Look at this workflow and identify what AI can draft, what software can automate, and what should stay human-controlled: [workflow].
I have [amount of time] to make progress on [goal]. Give me the smallest sequence of actions that produces a visible result today.

workflows.name: Research → Brief
steps: Define the exact question, audience, deadline, and what would count as a useful answer.
Gather current sources and separate facts from opinions or assumptions.
Extract the recurring findings, disagreements, numbers, and unanswered questions.
Ask AI to draft a structured brief using only the supplied evidence.
Review every important claim, tighten the brief, and add next actions.

workflows.name: Idea → Finished Content
steps: Describe the audience, platform, point of view, and desired action.
Generate several genuinely different angles before choosing one.
Create an outline with hook, value, proof/example, and CTA.
Draft the content, then run a separate clarity and retention edit.
Publish, record performance, and feed the result into the next iteration.

workflows.name: Messy Task → Repeatable System
steps: Write down how the task is actually performed today.
Separate triggers, inputs, decisions, actions, outputs, and exceptions.
Mark each step human, AI-assisted, or automatable.
Create the smallest safe workflow and define an approval checkpoint.
Test with one real case, record failures, and update the process.

workflows.name: Customer Problem → Offer
steps: Collect real customer language, complaints, questions, and desired outcomes.
Cluster the evidence into repeated problems and high-value outcomes.
Choose one problem and write a specific promise for one audience.
Build the smallest version of the offer that can test demand.
Put it in front of real people, measure response, and revise from evidence.

workflows.name: Big Goal → This Week
steps: Define what done looks like in observable terms.
List dependencies and the few actions that create the most progress.
Break those actions into tasks that fit your actual available time.
Schedule the first irreversible or visible action early.
End the week with a review: result, blocker, lesson, and next move.

footer: Use AI as a working partner, not an unquestioned authority. Check important facts, protect sensitive information, and make the final work your own. — Let Me Teach You AI
